description: Queries with no answer anywhere in the store, for measuring whether recall can tell it has nothing. Authored 2026-09-26. Each case's key terms were searched across every memory's topic and content first; where a term did occur the hit was read and found incidental. Cases whose premise a stored memory refutes (for instance 'the day agent-memory went public', answered by the memory on why it is private) were excluded: a refutation is an answer. off_domain asks about fields the store never covers; near_domain uses the store's own vocabulary for events that never happened, which is the hard half. Writing any of these queries into a memory file makes it answerable -- keep them out of hot and cold. Revised the same day after a cross-review: five cases were dropped because a memory answers or refutes them (Figma packaging; SQLite chosen over a heavier backend; the embedding model confirmed as kept; the hot/cold storage design; clean-up triggered by the user, not a timer). The first check matched exact key terms, which cannot see a memory that refutes a premise in other words.
